gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a dated, store-by-store price for the whole field, or says that Renogy's Voyager 20A PWM controller (the one built into ChatGPT's two Renogy picks) has to have its voltage set by hand to charge lithium, while ACOPOWER's 20A controller lists LiFePO4 among its 8 built-in battery types.
standout_why: Every result ChatGPT got (results 1–13) is a Renogy product page or a reseller copy of one, plus the Renogy STCS100D manual PDF, and none of them prices a rival. ChatGPT's cards then quoted prices that are now out of date. Renogy's own store lists the 100/200W suitcase from $229.99 against a $322.99 compare-at, and its 100W-only listing is $229.99, while the card showed $249.99 at Home Depot. VEVOR's own page has the 200W panel at $129.90, while the card showed $149.90 from a reseller. ChatGPT's answer tells the shopper to check LiFePO4 support but does not say which controllers have it. That detail is on Renogy's Voyager controller page and ACOPOWER's product pages, and none of the cited pages states it.
decides: This mostly backs ChatGPT's picks but changes the advice. For a 12 V lead-acid or AGM battery, the Renogy suitcase is fine, and it is cheapest from Renogy at $229.99, not Home Depot. For a LiFePO4 battery, ACOPOWER's kits (PLK from $219, or the 100 W ProteusX at $189) have a lithium preset, while Renogy's Voyager needs its voltage set by hand. For a power station, a panel with its own controller is the wrong buy: ACOPOWER says to bypass its controller for 'solar generators with a built-in charge controller'. A kit like the BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 + 100 W ($489.99), whose station has its own MPPT charger, is the better fit.
